clinicalPearls: Byssinosis is caused by inhaling dust from cotton, flax or hemp processing, classically in textile mill workers
The hallmark symptom is chest tightness and breathlessness that is worst on the first working day after a break, giving the classic 'Monday feeling' pattern
Early disease shows symptoms only on the first day back at work, whereas advanced disease brings symptoms on most working days and eventually persistent airflow limitation
Endotoxin from bacterial contamination of the raw fibre is thought to be a key causative component of the dust
The temporal work pattern is diagnostically important and is captured through a careful occupational history and grading of symptoms
Serial lung function across the working week, showing a fall in FEV1 over a shift, supports the diagnosis
Prevention through dust suppression, ventilation and exposure limits is the mainstay, since established chronic disease is not reversible
Chronic heavy exposure can lead to fixed obstructive impairment resembling chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
reference.pathophysiology: Inhalation of vegetable fibre dust, particularly cotton contaminated with bacterial endotoxin, triggers release of inflammatory mediators and acute airway narrowing. Repeated exposure produces recurrent bronchoconstriction that is initially reversible and tied to the work cycle, but sustained long-term exposure leads to chronic airway inflammation and persistent, largely irreversible airflow obstruction.
additionalDifferentials: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease from smoking
additionalInvestigations: Occupational history focusing on the first-day-of-week symptom pattern
Spirometry measured before and across a work shift to detect acute FEV1 decline
Serial peak flow monitoring over the working week
Symptom grading using recognised byssinosis classification
Chest imaging mainly to exclude other causes
redFlags: Progression from first-day symptoms to daily symptoms indicating chronic disease
Development of persistent breathlessness and fixed airflow obstruction
Acute severe respiratory distress after very heavy dust exposure
Superimposed respiratory infection worsening chronic impairment
reference.prognosis: Symptoms in early byssinosis may resolve with removal from exposure, but repeated and prolonged exposure can cause permanent obstructive lung impairment; the outlook improves substantially where dust exposure is controlled and workers are removed early.
pitfalls: Missing the characteristic first-working-day pattern by not asking about symptom timing
Attributing symptoms solely to smoking in a dust-exposed textile worker
Failing to act at the early reversible stage before fixed obstruction develops
Neglecting workplace dust control and surveillance of coworkers
